title: 倾听的姿态 / A Listening Tilt
input_provenance: AI-generated fictional young beagle photograph; no real person's pet is depicted.
workflow: Generate fictional photographic input, inspect it, then edit that exact image into a graphite-imprint artwork.

before.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create a single beautiful original editorial pet photograph of a fictional young tricolor beagle puppy sitting on a simple studio floor against a soft powder sky-blue seamless backdrop. Portrait 4:5. The puppy has warm chestnut-brown drooping ears, a brown face with a distinct slightly asymmetrical white blaze down the forehead and nose, a little white patch offset beside the nose, gentle round hazel-brown eyes, a black nose, white chest, two white front paws fully visible, and a black saddle on the back. A narrow simple vermilion-red fabric collar circles the neck with no lettering or tag. The head tilts just a little toward the viewer's left, conveying quiet curiosity; ears hang naturally on either side. Realistic young beagle proportions and short coat, not a toy or a doll. The puppy sits naturally, both front legs anatomically correct and separated by a little negative space, chest and forepaws not cropped, ears entirely within the frame. A small portion of a hind leg may be visible naturally, no extra limbs.

Composition: full seated puppy occupies roughly 75 percent of image height, balanced slightly below center with breathing room above the head and under the paws. A beautiful gentle rhythm of face, red collar and white paws. Camera near the puppy's eye level, looking slightly down just enough to see both forepaws; soft broad windowlike side light, very subtle ground contact shadow. High-quality natural editorial photography with true fur texture, wet but not overglossy nose, clear pupils and soft catchlights. Color palette powder blue, chestnut, ivory, deep black and a restrained red accent. Clean uncluttered studio feeling, emotionally warm and unforced. No props, plants, furniture, bones, toys, humans, hands, leash, text, signature, logo, border, collage or watermark. No exaggerated smiling mouth, no hypercute giant eyes, no plastic skin, no oversaturated HDR. Produce only the photograph.

after.prompt:
Edit the supplied photograph of the young beagle puppy into a refined 'Soul Imprint / 灵魂拓印' artwork: a luminous selective graphite impression on clean thin white paper. The original photograph is the exact identity and composition authority. Preserve this SAME beagle's head tilt, round gentle eyes, long soft ear silhouettes and unequal ear angles, the asymmetrical narrow white blaze, white muzzle shape, black nose, seated proportions, position of the simple collar, two visible front paws and the visible rear paw at the lower right. Keep the original portrait 4:5 framing, body scale, and natural sitting stance. It must remain unmistakably the same young beagle, not a different breed, an older hound, or a cartoon dog.

Transform the medium rather than merely desaturating the photograph. Render the face with a few selective graphite accents: dark nose and the upper eye edges, subtle iris/pupil tones, a few softly deposited muzzle details. Preserve the alive, curious tenderness of its expression, with paper-white highlights and no black hollow eye sockets. Transfer the chestnut ear and forehead regions into uneven grey impressions made of short directional patches, delicate granular edges and missing paper-white gaps, following the flow of the short coat without drawing every hair. Several edges of the ears may fragment while their overall hanging shape remains legible. The white blaze, chest and forelegs become large areas of untouched white paper, bounded only by occasional silvery traces. The black saddle is retained as a compact stronger dark impression on the upper side of the torso, then breaks apart toward the lower flank.

The collar stays in its original neck position as a small charcoal-grey curved band with broken weave texture; remove its red color. Give it enough presence to connect the head and body without turning it into a thick black ring. Let substantial portions of the chest, outside foreleg contours, lower torso and rear haunch genuinely disappear into the white sheet, while leaving a few paw-toe and leg-placement traces to maintain anatomy. A few strong marks, interrupted medium grey passages, and fully blank paper must coexist. Do not make a uniformly pale pencil portrait. Avoid fully continuous silhouettes, dense cross-hatching, photorealistic fur shading or a global grunge overlay. The head and ear rhythm is the primary focus; the tapering body and little paws grow quieter below it.

The blue studio background and floor disappear completely into fresh neutral-to-slightly-cool white kozo-like paper with fine fibers visible only close up. Keep surrounding blank areas clean and still. No sepia, brown staining, all-over wrinkles, smoky haze or distressed border. No actual dog standing on a sheet, no object cast shadow, no simulation of an animal being pressed or wrapped. No tears, scars, funerary mood, skeleton or medical imagery; the dog stays warm and friendly. No title, text, labels, signature, frame, drawing tools, hands, added props, colored areas or before/after layout. Produce only the finished graphite-imprint artwork, at the same orientation as the supplied photograph.

quality_notes: The young beagle's head tilt, soft drooping ears, asymmetric white blaze, curious gaze, collar position and seated paw geometry remain recognizable. Chest and leg surfaces open into blank paper while the face and saddle retain stronger impressions. No additional revision used.
